children: shares fell 2.8% at 10.45 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, after SpaceX shares rose overnight. Yahoo Finance reported that Barclays sees an all-stock deal with SpaceX buying Tesla as the most likely outcome of merger talks, with Tesla holders receiving SpaceX shares. No formal filing, terms or exchange ratio have been disclosed.

The process is still early. Elon Musk has said independent directors are handling the talks, that he is a conflicted party excluded from special committee discussions, and that holders of 50% of outstanding Tesla shares would need to approve. He has cited AI, robotics and the companies' joint chipmaking project, Terafab, as reasons to combine. Tesla's latest operating update showed third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 vehicles and 13.7 GWh of energy storage deployed.

With Tesla's market cap near $1.5 trillion and the combined value near $3.5 trillion, Tesla holders would own well under half of a merged group at market-based terms. Inference: that dilution of control, not deal logic, is why Tesla is trading lower while SpaceX holds up. GuruFocus gives Tesla a GF Score of 87/100, strong on balance sheet and growth but weaker on profitability. At $380.35, shares trade about 6% above the $359.83 GF Value, which GuruFocus labels fairly valued. The next measurable step is any special committee filing that names advisers, terms or a timeline.

title: Tesla Stocks Fall 2.8% as SpaceX Merger Talk Turns to Who Buys Whom
